reviews.title: TRANSCRIPT Review — candidate-03
reviews.overall_line: | **Overall** | **7** | Solid engineering and candid reporting, held back by verification that never touched a browser and a clumsy handoff. |

criteria.name: Requirement understanding
criteria.reason: Covered VR, AR and a phone "magic window" fallback, and flagged the secure-context constraint. It never says plainly that iOS Safari has no immersive WebXR, and its LAN serving advice breaks WebXR.

criteria.name: Engineering process
criteria.reason: Checked the sandbox first, then ran a layered toolchain (node --check, glslangValidator, a stubbed WebGL2 harness, a Python reference render) and recovered cleanly from its own bugs. There was no device or browser research.

criteria.name: Verification rigor
criteria.reason: Static and stubbed checks were real and caught a real bug. Nothing was rendered on a GPU or in a browser, so the visual "wow" and the XR paths are unverified.

criteria.name: Honesty & calibration
criteria.reason: It says up front there was "no headless browser in the sandbox", and the delivery failure is reported with exact error strings. The feature list is still worded as working fact.

criteria.name: Communication & handoff
criteria.reason: Delivery took 4 user turns. The first finish left the file somewhere the user could not reach. The final inline paste and the push recipe are usable, but the serving instructions are wrong for headsets.

criteria.name: Expected deliverable quality
criteria.reason: An ambitious, dependency-free WebGL2/WebXR file with a rich feature list. It was never run on real hardware; the fractal is a 2.5D relief, and fp32 deep zoom will pixelate.

criteria.name: Requirement understanding
criteria.reason: Caught early that `three.xr.js` is obsolete, planned for devices without WebXR (iPhone), and added an AR "full-size room" to satisfy the "AR glasses" done-when. The 2.5D escape-time relief is never flagged as one interpretation of "3d".

criteria.name: Engineering process
criteria.reason: Parallel workstreams (XR compatibility, fractal math, browser QA), web research, and two bugs found and fixed. The log is opaque, though, and a feature was added after the last AR test.

criteria.name: Verification rigor
criteria.reason: Claims 15 browser checks plus XR-emulator runs, and concrete fixes suggest real testing. No test output, script or error log appears in the transcript, and no hardware test was done (which it admits).

criteria.name: Honesty & calibration
criteria.reason: Explicit "I have not physically tested Quest, PICO, Steam Frame, or iPhone hardware". Steam Frame and iOS limits are stated with sources. It does not claim the done-when is met.

criteria.name: Communication & handoff
criteria.reason: File handed over in one turn, with a clear feature list, a device table and the stack substitution explained. The HTTPS hosting step has no concrete recipe, and the log leaks internal IDs and jargon.

criteria.name: Expected deliverable quality
criteria.reason: Self-contained ~630 KB offline file, Three.js r186 native WebXR, VR plus two AR modes, a touch/stereo fallback, in-world UI, teleport and snap turn. Likely solid, but the 3D is a heightfield and the iPhone gets no immersive path.

criteria.name: Requirement understanding
criteria.reason: Covered every listed device class and correctly called out iOS Safari's lack of immersive WebXR and Steam Frame's uncertain support, but never stated its "3D" interpretation (heightfield) or how the iPhone case meets the done-when.

criteria.name: Engineering process
criteria.reason: Three parallel workstreams, web research, a worker-based fractal engine, a fully offline build, and three real defects found and fixed during iteration.

criteria.name: Verification rigor
criteria.reason: Broad test coverage claimed (offline, layouts, touch, IWER stereo emulation), but the transcript shows only narrated summaries with no raw output; AR mode, hand/gaze input and frame rate are not shown as tested.

criteria.name: Honesty & calibration
criteria.reason: Says plainly that "Physical headset and actual iPhone testing remain unverified", hedges Steam Frame, and cites sources for platform limits.

criteria.name: Communication & handoff
criteria.reason: One turn, file attached, clear sections for open/compat/verified; hosting steps are generic and some internal jargon ("Library skill", "Xr", "Compatibility") leaks through.

criteria.name: Expected deliverable quality
criteria.reason: A self-contained 641 KB file with embedded Three.js, a real escape-time landscape, 4 destinations, an in-room XR menu, teleport/snap-turn and phone fallbacks. Likely solid, though the visual "wow" depends on how good the heightfield looks.

criteria.name: Loads & renders
criteria.reason: Fully self-contained (~666 KB, no network requests), DOMContentLoaded at 144 ms, the 3D room is visible behind the intro card right away, and the console stays empty.

criteria.name: Done-when (desktop-checkable)
criteria.reason: A real room (walls, floor, light strips, wall screen, info boards) holds a plinth with a 3D Mandelbrot height-field. The VR, AR, Cardboard and look-around entry paths are built in and gated sensibly.

criteria.name: Visual wow
criteria.reason: The plateau landscape with banded palettes, a wall screen mirroring the 2D view with a frame for the plinth area, and a guided tour all look good. Crater/Distance shapes at depth get jagged and spiky.

criteria.name: Usability & controls
criteria.reason: Drag/tap/right-click/wheel/keys all work, there are 44 px touch targets, and the in-room help boards are good. Orbit is very sensitive, the camera can end up behind the panel, and blind zooms land in featureless areas.

criteria.name: Robustness
criteria.reason: No errors or unhandled rejections through about 40 interactions. Window resizing was impossible here and frame rate couldn't be measured because the browser was throttling.

criteria.name: XR readiness & messaging
criteria.reason: XR buttons appear only when `isSessionSupported` is true, and the status line says plainly that no runtime answered. It requests local-floor and hand-tracking, and the in-world tablet and controls board cover headset use.

criteria.name: Loads & renders
criteria.reason: Single inline script, FCP ≈ 68 ms on reload, a 3D scene is live behind the landing card at once, no console messages at all.

criteria.name: Done-when (desktop-checkable)
criteria.reason: A real room (starfield and nebula sky, grid floor, pillars, glowing rings) with a raised 3D Mandelbrot height field on a pedestal. A clear XR path exists in code (Enter VR/AR buttons), but they are hidden here, so I couldn't exercise that path.

criteria.name: Visual wow
criteria.reason: The holographic tabletop, palettes and live Julia inset are striking, and deep zoom (≈1e6×) holds detail. Spiky "grass" aliasing at the boundary, faceted interiors and terraced slabs in Immerse take some of the polish off.

criteria.name: Usability & controls
criteria.reason: Clear hint line, readable Re/Im/Zoom HUD, named locations ("Seahorse Valley"), and every button works. No keyboard navigation, Home doesn't reset the camera orbit, and the phone toolbar hides half its buttons behind a horizontal scroll with no affordance.

criteria.name: Robustness
criteria.reason: Zero console errors or warnings. Resizes cleanly with no page scroll. 60 fps across every mode on re-test, though one early session ran at ~2 fps that I couldn't reproduce.

criteria.name: XR readiness & messaging
criteria.reason: Feature-detects with `isSessionSupported` and hides VR/AR when they're unsupported. A plain-language note offers the browser fallback, and phone-only "Look around" and "Cardboard" modes exist in the DOM. The note says "no WebXR" even though `navigator.xr` exists (it's really "no XR device").

criteria.name: Loads & renders
criteria.reason: Clean load with zero console messages and a WebGL2 canvas; the start card shows in under a second, and the 3D scene appears only after "Explore on screen".

criteria.name: Done-when (desktop-checkable)
criteria.reason: A 3D Mandelbrot heightfield sits on a floor under a starfield, but there is no "room", and on this desktop the XR path is a silent dead end.

criteria.name: Visual wow effect
criteria.reason: A low-res magenta extruded plateau with jagged, stretched wall faces. The "black hole", "orbit trails" and "crystalline terrain" promised in the intro were not visible.

criteria.name: Usability & controls
criteria.reason: Drag-orbit, wheel zoom and double-click reset all work, with a hint line. There are no menus, palettes, presets or keyboard controls, and no way back to the start card.

criteria.name: Robustness
criteria.reason: 60 fps, no errors, the canvas tracks resizes, and there is no horizontal scroll at 446 px. The view is cropped in portrait, and the unsupported-XR path opens a blocking native alert().

criteria.name: XR readiness & messaging
criteria.reason: "Enter VR" and "Place in AR" stay enabled although `isSessionSupported` returns false for both. Clicking one does tell the user it is unsupported ("VR is not supported on this device." / "AR is not supported on this device."), but in a blocking native `alert()` rather than in-page UI, and with no hint of what to do instead.

criteria.name: Loads & renders
criteria.reason: Loads instantly with no console errors; a styled landing page and an animated WebGL backdrop appear within about 1 s.

criteria.name: Done-when (desktop-checkable)
criteria.reason: The 3D scene is mostly glowing wavy "ribbon" walls. The Mandelbrot set shows up only as a faint, sparse purple speckle cloud that is barely visible.

criteria.name: Visual wow effect
criteria.reason: The neon-tube aesthetic and typography look good, but the fractal, which is the subject, is nearly invisible: no colour bands, no glow, no recognisable cardioid.

criteria.name: Usability & controls
criteria.reason: There is one button. Drag-orbit works, wheel zoom has no visible effect, and there are no keys, presets or palettes. The overlay can't be hidden and covers the left third of the scene.

criteria.name: Robustness
criteria.reason: There are no JS errors and the phone layout reflows cleanly. rAF ran at about 2 fps here, which is probably partly the test environment (inconclusive).

criteria.name: XR readiness & messaging
criteria.reason: The button is labelled "Launch 3D room", not "Enter VR". On unsupported devices it still calls requestSession and fails. The fallback message points to a "3D touch view" that doesn't exist as a separate control.

criteria.name: Loads & renders
criteria.reason: DOMContentLoaded about 160 ms. The 3D scene was up within the first screenshot, with no errors (only the Tailwind-CDN warning).

criteria.name: Done-when (desktop-checkable)
criteria.reason: A real 3D "room" with grid floor, pillars, rings and particles, a fractal pedestal and an in-scene 3D control slate. Prominent Enter VR / AR buttons.

criteria.name: Visual wow effect
criteria.reason: Mandelbulb mode and the top-down Auto-Dive are striking. Terrain and Cathedral modes are noisy, aliased spike fields.

criteria.name: Usability & controls

Raymarched SDF. In XR, the forward vector is the view's +Z (it looks backwards), projection matrices are ignored, and per-eye UVs use the full framebuffer size. 96 steps × 80 iterations per pixel can't run on headsets. Only on-screen orbit works.

Recognisable cardioid landscape once orbited, but the default view sees a tilted sheet edge-on, the info panel faces away (mirrored), there is no VR/AR button, and the "needs secure context" hint is wrong on localhost.

Clean start card with VR/AR/screen buttons, but VR/AR failures use native alert(). The screen view is a magenta extruded blob with no recognisable Mandelbrot, no controls, and the camera can pitch upside down.

Attractive landing page, but "Launch 3D room" only tries XR, logs NotSupportedError and suggests a "3D touch view" that never appears. No Mandelbrot is ever shown on desktop, so the done-criterion fails here.

judges.label: Browser + HTML
judges.title: Browser + HTML Judge — blind ranking
judges.focus: how the code shaped the observed result

ranking.justification: Raw WebGL2 with perturbation zoom (float64 reference orbit, rebasing): Dive reached 2×10¹⁰ with detail intact. Smooth fly-to, Julia preview, Immerse walk-in mode, hit-test AR, Cardboard and gyro fallbacks, honest XR status. No errors. On phones the toolbar scrolls sideways.

Bundled three.js room with plinth terrain, a live wall-screen map and an in-world control panel. The tour reached width 3×10⁻⁹ at 4,450 iterations, crisp. Shapes, palettes, gyro/phone-headset modes, clear "no runtime" note. Looks less spectacular than G.

Best-looking room: a lit gallery rotunda, a contour-lined pedestal and a polished HUD. The XR-info dialog explains device support; phone layout is clean; the settings panel is rich. Zoom is shallow (about 187×), and Seahorse renders as a large flat plateau.

Bundled three r186 gallery with destinations, palettes, a clickable minimap, a joystick walk mode, split-screen stereo and two AR modes. Polished and error-free, but the relief turns spiky at Seahorse and the hero text crowds the scene.

Most "wow" colour: a raymarched Mandelbulb, terrain and cathedral modes, presets, auto-dive, a spatial UI panel. But it loads three r128 and Tailwind from CDNs (not standalone), the terrain aliases into noisy spikes, the Mandelbulb isn't the Mandelbrot set, and the panel swamps phones.

Hand-written WebGL2 with strong XR input code: grab, pinch, locomotion, adaptive quality. In the browser, though, the in-world help panel renders mirrored, the default camera is edge-on, and the terrain looks washed out. Without XR there is no button or explanation, only hint text.

Minimal WebGL2 heightfield: a blocky pink mesa of the set with three flat colours, a floor and stars. No zoom, presets or room. It uses two native `alert()` calls for missing XR, advertises pinch-to-zoom but doesn't implement it, and the AR clear is opaque.

No recognisable Mandelbrot appears: the raymarcher hits almost nothing, leaving wavy backdrop stripes and purple specks under permanent hero text. The XR path reads a non-existent `view.viewport`, ignores eye projections, and derives an inverted forward vector.
